claims.text: Introducing a refractory element can improve the structural stability of a high-entropy nanoalloy at high temperature.
Introducing a refractory element can improve the chemical stability of a high-entropy nanoalloy at high temperature.
Introducing a refractory element leads to the formation of a stable refractory phase.
The stable refractory phase acts as a barrier to diffusion.
The stable refractory phase acts as a barrier to oxidation.
Suppression of diffusion and oxidation improves resistance to alloy degradation.
A high-entropy nanoalloy containing a refractory element will have better structural stability than an otherwise comparable alloy without that refractory element.
A high-entropy nanoalloy containing a refractory element will have better chemical stability than an otherwise comparable alloy without that refractory element.
The predicted improvement should hold over 500–1000 °C.
The effectiveness of refractory-element addition may depend on the identity of the refractory element.
The effectiveness of refractory-element addition may depend on its concentration in the alloy.
